name: Gryphon Roost
summary: Gryphons take travelers from Stormwind’s eastern ramparts across the Eastern Kingdoms. Dungar Longdrink, a human gryphon master, manages the roost beside the Trade District.

sections.title: Gateway to the Skies
sections.body: From the eastern ramparts, gryphons carry travelers from Stormwind to Alliance garrisons and settlements across the Eastern Kingdoms. Dungar Longdrink, the seasoned gryphon master, coordinates flights to Ironforge, Lakeshire, Sentinel Hill, and other destinations.

sections.title: A Touch of the Aerie
sections.body: Gryphons and their handlers bring a trace of Hinterlands tradition within Stormwind’s walls. The Wildhammer clan has long revered gryphons as partners and introduced aerial warfare and transport to the broader Alliance during the Second War. Leather, feed, and fresh winds mark the roost amid the city’s stonework.

faq.q: Where is the Gryphon Roost located in Stormwind?
faq.answer: The Gryphon Roost sits on Stormwind’s eastern ramparts, reached by a stairway from the Trade District. It overlooks the canals between the Trade District and Old Town.
Dungar Longdrink, a human flight master, manages the roost’s flights. He organizes routes and rents trained gryphons to travelers bound for allied settlements across the continent.

faq.q: Why are dwarves running the roost in a human city?
faq.answer: Stormwind’s flight master, Dungar Longdrink, is human. The Wildhammer dwarves have a long tradition of gryphon riding, while Dungar manages the roost’s flights.

faq.q: Where can the gryphons fly from here?
faq.answer: The roost connects Stormwind with Alliance destinations including Sentinel Hill, Lakeshire, Darkshire, and Ironforge. Other routes reach settlements across the Eastern Kingdoms.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you can see your people’s long tradition of gryphon riding carried into Stormwind. Trained gryphons connect the human capital with Khaz Modan.
As an Alliance traveler, you can carry messages by air from Stormwind to territories such as Westfall and Redridge, helping coordinate responses there.
